expert_reviews.title: Yamaha R15 V4: Roadtest Review
expert_reviews.description: We have ridden the Yamaha R15 V4 previously, albeit for a short period wherein we couldn’t exploit the full potential of the heavy updates it has received. So, we did this time, and here is what we came back with.

reviews.title: R15 Dual Tone Quick shifter
reviews.description: I purchased this bike in February 2026 from Rohtak. I love its body shape and color combination. The meter is good, and the halogen lights are fabulous; they make the night look as bright as day. This bike is amazing for couples, and it's also great for solo rides. I highly recommend buying it! ❤️

reviews.title: Review on r15
reviews.description: Handling is one of the R15’s biggest strengths. The Deltabox frame and USD front forks provide excellent stability and cornering confidence. Features like dual-channel ABS, traction control, and a quick shifter (in higher variants) add to its appeal.</br>However, the aggressive riding posture may feel uncomfortable in city traffic, and pillion comfort is limited. With a mileage of around 40–50 km/l, the R15 balances performance and efficiency well, making it ideal for young enthusiasts seeking a sporty ride.

reviews.title: R15 wale
reviews.description: I bought the Yamaha R15 because I wanted a sporty bike with good mileage and strong performance. The buying experience was smooth and the showroom staff explained everything properly. The first thing you notice is the aggressive look — it feels like a mini superbike. The riding posture is sporty but still comfortable for daily use if you get used to it.</br>Performance is the best part. The engine is smooth, pickup is quick, and cornering feels very stable. On highways, it feels confident and planted. Mileage is also decent for a sports bike if you ride properly. The servicing cost is reasonable, and the Yamaha service center are reliable. Maintenance is easy if you service on time and keep the chain clean and lubricated.</br>Pros are amazing looks, great handling, strong braking, and good mileage. Cons are slightly hard seats for long rides and a committed riding posture in traffic. My tip is to always warm up the engine, clean the chain regularly, and use good-quality engine oil for long life. Overall, R15 is perfect for young riders who want style with performance.

reviews.title: THE MOST HONEST REVIEW OF R15 V4

Whether it's dual ABS technology which saves in the high speed and urgent braking situations and killers looks. Just two downsides, for daily city rides it's uncomfortable due to frequent brakes and turns plus mileage in the city is low.. 44kmpl is the max you could expect and for highways it's way better... It's like for clear highways this baby gives 60+ kmpl often.

reviews.title: Looks+Performance+mileage = Yamaha R15
reviews.description: After spending 40,000 km in the saddle of my Yamaha R15M, I can confidently say this isn’t just a "small-capacity" bike—it’s a precision tool. Here’s how it has held up over the years.</br>1. Aesthetics: Still a Head-Turner</br>Even after 40k km, the R1M-inspired design remains the best-looking in its class.</br>Presence: The metallic silver finish and the M-branding still get plenty of attention at traffic lights.</br>Build Quality: Despite the high mileage, the fairings haven't developed major rattles, and the paint quality has held up surprisingly well against the elements.</br>2. Performance: The VVA Magic</br>The 155cc engine is a gem that loves to be pushed.</br>Engine Refinement: Even at 40,000 km, the engine feels "broken in" rather than "worn out." The Variable Valve Actuation (VVA) still kicks in seamlessly at 7,400 RPM, giving that signature top-end surge.</br>Quickshifter: This is the highlight of the M variant. Up-shifts remain crisp and make city riding or spirited highway runs incredibly engaging.</br>Handling: The USD forks and the Deltabox frame still provide razor-sharp handling. It carves corners just as well today as it did on Day 1.</br>3. Mileage: The "Pocket-Friendly" Sports Bike</br>One of the most impressive parts of this journey has been the fuel efficiency.</br>City: I consistently get around 40–43 km/l even in moderate traffic.</br>Highway: If you cruise around 80–90 km/h, it’s easy to see 50+ km/l.</br>Range: With its 11L tank, I rarely worry about frequent fuel stops during long tours.</br>4. Maintenance & Reliability</br>Reliability: I’ve had zero major engine breakdowns. Stick to the service intervals, and this bike is bulletproof.</br>Wear & Tear: Over 40k km, I’ve gone through roughly 2 sets of tires and 3 sets of brake pads. I recommend upgrading to stickier tires (like Apollo Alpha H1 or Michelin) for better wet-weather grip.</br>🚩 The Minor Cons</br>Aggressive Posture: It’s a committed stance. After 40,000 km, my wrists are used to it, but it’s not a bike for those who prioritize comfort over sportiness.</br>Pillion Comfort: As always, the rear seat is strictly for short distances.</br>Final Verdict</br>The Yamaha R15M is the perfect balance of premium looks, track-level performance, and commuter-level mileage. If you maintain it well, 40,000 km is just the beginning.

expert_reviews.title: Yamaha FZ-S V3: Road Test Review
expert_reviews.description: It all started with the FZ-16 that was introduced in India back in 2008. It was the bike all the young guns wanted. Fast forward to 2019 and here you have the FZ-S V3 which, as the insightful lot of you might have guessed right, is the third generation of the FZ-16. How much has changed over the years? Is it still…the ‘Lord of the Streets’?

reviews.title: Good comuter bike
reviews.description: Riding experience is very good. I have done several long tours on this bike, and it feels comfortable and stable on highways as well as city roads. Maintenance cost is reasonable. However, after around two year,s I started facing a starting issue occasionally, especially in the morning. Needs fixing..

reviews.title: Value of your money
reviews.description: The Yamaha FZ FI is one of those motorcycles that proves you don’t need a massive engine to have a satisfying riding experience. Designed primarily for city riders, it blends style, efficiency, and everyday practicality in a way that makes it a favourite among commuters and beginners alike.</br>First off, the design is a big win. The muscular fuel tank, sharp tank shrouds, and compact tail section give the FZ FI a sporty, big-bike feel despite its smaller engine. The LED headlamp and digital instrument cluster add a modern touch, making the bike look premium for its segment.</br>Under the hood, the fuel-injected engine is tuned for smooth and predictable performance rather than outright speed. Acceleration is linear, which makes riding in traffic stress-free. The throttle response is clean, and the bike rarely feels jerky, even at low speeds. It’s not built for high-speed highway thrills, but for daily city rides, it’s more than capable.</br>One of the strongest points of the FZ FI is comfort. The upright riding posture, wide handlebars, and well-cushioned seat make long commutes surprisingly easy on the back and shoulders. The suspension setup handles potholes and rough patches reasonably well, which is a big plus on uneven roads.</br>Mileage is another highlight. The fuel-injection system ensures efficient fuel use, making the FZ FI light on the pocket in the long run. Maintenance is also relatively simple, and Yamaha’s reliability adds peace of mind.</br>Handling is nimble and confidence-inspiring. The bike feels stable in corners and easy to manoeuvre in tight traffic. Braking performance, especially with disc brakes and ABS (in newer versions), is reassuring.</br>Overall, the Yamaha FZ FI is a stylish, comfortable, and reliable commuter that perfectly balances performance and practicality.

reviews.title: Good bike

The best part of the bike is the riding posture, which is very comfortable and has smooth seats. Lacking in power production, which is not as expected. This is my first bike it's a great 1st bike anyone can buy but after 8k km i started to feel like i need more power especially in long rides probably a 200cc or 250cc will be better. if you are planning to buy only for city commutes go for it, it's great bike for city usage but i don't recommed those who are picking this for long drive above 250km

expert_reviews.description: We have ridden the Yamaha FZ-X extensively, even having it as our long-termer for three months and you can read all about it by clicking here. However, here’s a summary of our review telling you the hits and misses of the FZ-X.

expert_reviews.description: Yes, the FZ-X’s affinity to the city was quite pronounced. But even with its supposedly adventure-ish persona, one will most definitely use it to commute the most. So, allow me to spell out the things I liked about the FZ-X and the things I wished were better during my time with the motorcycle.

expert_reviews.title: Yamaha FZ-X Long Term Review: Introduction
expert_reviews.description: Seemingly confident about their product, Yamaha sent us the FZ-X to use for over a month. And in this time, I am looking forward to seeing how it performs on daily commutes and tours. I will also be looking to see if the Yamaha FZ-X feels like a settlement over the XSR155 that has achieved celebrity status in India- or, at least online.

expert_reviews.title: Yamaha FZ-X: First Ride Review
expert_reviews.description: This is a Yamaha motorcycle and as you can see it has some neo-modern retro styling and also some bits that makes it look tough and rugged. But it is not the XSR 155. It is the Indianized version of it and it goes by the name the FZ-X.

reviews.title: A Stylish and Comfortable Daily Ride
reviews.description: I’ve been riding the Yamaha FZ-X for a while now, and it feels solid and comfortable for daily use. The seating is upright, suspension is smooth, and mileage is decent, around 45 kmpl in the city. It’s not very powerful, but for relaxed rides and stylish looks, it’s a good, reliable choice. A Stylish and Comfortable Daily Ride

reviews.title: Comfort

reviews.title: Best experience
reviews.description: I recently spent some time riding the Yamaha FZ-X, and it has been a surprisingly enjoyable experience. Right from the moment I sat on it, the upright seating posture felt comfortable, giving me full control over the handlebars without feeling stretched or cramped. The seat is wide and soft, making longer rides less tiring, and even on bumpy city roads, the suspension does a great job absorbing shocks.</br>The 149cc engine isn’t about blazing speed, but it’s smooth, predictable, and responsive for city commuting. Acceleration feels adequate for overtaking in traffic, and the gearbox is light and precise. I especially liked how easy it is to manoeuvre through tight lanes thanks to its lightweight chassis.</br>On longer stretches, the bike feels stable and planted, though it’s not meant for very high-speed touring. The LED headlamp is bright, making night rides safer, and the digital console is easy to read while riding. Fuel efficiency is impressive, and I was getting around 45–48 kmpl in mixed riding.</br>Overall, riding the FZ-X feels relaxed and stress-free. It’s not just a bike; it’s a reliable companion for daily commuting and casual rides, with a style that always turns heads.

reviews.title: Worst experience
reviews.description: Extremely Disappointing Purchase Experience – Request for Resolution</br>I am writing to express my deep dissatisfaction with the service I received at your Rameswaram showroom during the purchase of my Yamaha FZX.</br>I was initially given a quotation for the FZX Hybrid model, based on which I paid an initial booking amount of ₹1,000.</br>The next day, I was informed that the hybrid model would cost an additional ₹10,000, which was never mentioned earlier. Because of this sudden change, I decided to switch to the standard (Phase) model.</br>The colour I wanted was not available at the Rameswaram showroom, and I was asked to pay an additional ₹1,000 for transferring the booking.</br>I clearly informed the team that I needed the vehicle on 23rd October by 10 AM, but I received it only at 7:30 PM, causing me significant inconvenience.</br> Before delivery, I had already paid 75% of the vehicle amount. Four days later, I completed the full payment, but I was still not given the invoice. I was told that the invoice would be provided after registration. Today, when I finally received the invoice, I was shocked to see a difference of around ₹10,000 compared to the original quote.</br>This entire experience—from misleading information, extra charges, delayed delivery, and lack of transparency—has been the worst showroom experience I have ever had.</br>I request a clear explanation for the price difference and the refund of any unjustified extra amount charged.

reviews.title: Hero Splendor Review – A Reliable Bike for Daily Use
reviews.description: I have been using my Hero Splendor bike for a long time, mainly for daily travel like going to college, office, and local work. My overall experience with this bike has been very good. The biggest advantage of the Splendor is its excellent mileage. Even with regular city riding, it gives very good fuel efficiency, which helps save money on petrol.</br>The bike is smooth to ride and easy to control in traffic. The seat is comfortable, and the suspension works well on rough and uneven roads. I do not feel tired even after long rides. The engine performance is simple but reliable, and it does not create much noise. Maintenance cost is low, and spare parts are easily available everywhere. This bike may not look very stylish or fast, but for daily use, Hero Splendor is a dependable and stress-free choice.

reviews.title: The Timeless Mileage King Meets Modern
reviews.description: The Hero Splendor Plus XTEC is a masterclass in practical commuting, successfully blending its legendary reputation for reliability with modern-day essentials. The driving experience is defined by its light 112 kg kerb weight, which makes it incredibly agile and easy to flick through congested city lanes. Comfort is a highlight for daily office runs, thanks to a well-padded seat and an upright riding posture that reduces back strain, though the suspension can feel a bit stiff over sharp potholes. Performance-wise, the 97.2cc engine is a refined workhorse that remains silent at low speeds, though vibrations become noticeable once you cross the 165 km/h mark. Its greatest strength is undeniably the mileage, consistently delivering 65–70 km/l in real-world conditions. The XTEC upgrade adds a layer of sophistication with a fully digital console, Bluetooth alerts, and a USB charger, which are rare luxuries in this segment. While the build quality is rugged enough 1 for rural roads, some owners have noted minor rusting on chrome parts if not maintained. Hero’s after-sales service remains its biggest competitive advantage, offering the most affordable spare parts and a vast network that ensures a hassle-free ownership experience for years.

reviews.title: Attractive Bike
reviews.description: The Hero Passion Pro is one of the most popular commuter motorcycles in India, known for its reliability, fuel efficiency, and stylish design. Manufactured by Hero MotoCorp, the Passion Pro has been designed especially for daily commuters who want a balance of performance, comfort, and affordability.</br>One of the biggest strengths of the Hero Passion Pro is its excellent mileage, which makes it an ideal choice for people who travel long distances every day. The bike is equipped with a 110cc engine that provides smooth performance and good pickup for city riding. The engine is refined and reliable, ensuring that riders experience minimal vibrations and consistent performance over time. Because of its fuel-efficient engine, the Passion Pro can deliver an impressive mileage of around 60–70 km per litre, making it economical for everyday use.</br>In terms of design, the Hero Passion Pro has a sporty and modern look that appeals to young riders as well as working professionals. The bike features stylish graphics, a sleek fuel tank, and attractive alloy wheels that give it a premium appearance despite being a commuter motorcycle. The comfortable seat and upright riding position make it suitable for long rides as well as daily office commutes.</br>Another important feature of the Hero Passion Pro is its comfort and handling. The bike is lightweight and easy to control, which makes it perfect for riding in heavy city traffic. The suspension system absorbs bumps and rough roads effectively, providing a smooth riding experience. Additionally, the braking system is responsive and reliable, ensuring rider safety.</br>The Passion Pro also comes with several modern features, such as an i3S (Idle Stop-Start System) technology that helps save fuel by automatically turning off the engine when the bike is idle and restarting it when the clutch is pressed. This feature improves fuel efficiency and makes the bike more environmentally friendly.</br>Overall, the Hero Passion Pro is a practical, stylish, and fuel-efficient motorcycle that meets the needs of everyday riders. With its dependable engine, comfortable ride quality, and affordable maintenance costs, it continues to be one of the most trusted commuter bikes in India. It is an excellent choice for students, office workers, and anyone looking for a reliable two-wheeler for daily transportation.

reviews.title: My point of view
reviews.description: Riding the Honda Shine 100 DX feels simple, calm, and practical, especially for daily commuting. From the moment you start the bike, the engine feels smooth and quiet, which gives confidence even to new riders. The clutch is light, and the gearbox shifts easily, making stop-and-go city traffic less tiring. On busy roads, the bike feels very manageable because of its lightweight body and balanced design.</br>While riding at city speeds around 40–60 km/h, the bike feels comfortable and stable. It is not built for speed or aggressive riding, but it performs well for regular office or college travel. On highways, you can cruise comfortably, though overtaking needs planning due to limited power. Vibrations are minimal at normal speeds, which adds to the overall riding comfort.</br>One of the best parts of the Shine 100 DX experience is its fuel efficiency. You don’t constantly worry about fuel, as the mileage is excellent in real-world conditions. This makes it very economical for daily use. The seat is soft, and the upright riding posture keeps your back relaxed even during longer rides. The suspension handles normal city roads and small potholes decently.</br>However, the bike feels basic in some areas. The drum brakes are average and need careful use, especially during sudden stops. The headlight is sufficient for city riding, but not very strong for night highways. Feature-wise, it focuses more on utility than modern technology.</br>Overall, the Honda Shine 100 DX feels like a dependable companion rather than an exciting machine. It is ideal for riders who want peace of mind, low running costs, and Honda’s reliability. If your priority is daily commuting with comfort and mileage, the Shine 100 DX delivers a satisfying experience.

expert_reviews.title: Honda Livo: First Ride Review
expert_reviews.description: The Honda Livo was recently launched as a spiritual successor to the CB Twister. Sold alongside the Dream series of 110cc commuter bikes, the Livo is the most expensive small-capacity commuter in the Japanese manufacturer’s line-up. While the Twister was one of the most stylish 110cc commuter motorcycles in the Indian market, it failed to capture the buyers’ imagination. Honda has attempted to overcome this defeat by taking a toned down approach towards styling, which despite being less flamboyant than the CB Twister, makes the Livo look like a true blue-blooded steed.

reviews.title: The Perfect Blend of Mileage and Reliability
reviews.description: I have been riding my Honda Livo Disc for the past 6 years, and it has been an extremely reliable partner throughout my journey. From daily office commutes to market runs and occasional long rides, this bike has never disappointed me.</br>The 110cc engine is smooth, refined, and very consistent even after years of use. Even today, the engine feels reliable and starts without any trouble. It may not be a high-speed performance bike, but for city riding, it delivers enough power for easy overtakes and smooth acceleration. What I appreciate most is the low vibration and stable performance even after long rides.</br>One of the biggest highlights of my Livo is its fuel efficiency. Even after 6 years, it still gives me around 60 kmpl, which is impressive. This makes it very economical and perfect for daily commuting. Maintenance costs have also been reasonable, and regular servicing keeps the bike in good condition.</br>The front disc brake provides confident braking, especially in sudden traffic situations. The suspension is comfortable and absorbs most bumps on rough roads. The seating posture is upright and comfortable for both rider and pillion, making longer rides less tiring.</br>In terms of design, the bike still looks stylish and simple. It is lightweight and easy to handle in city traffic. reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.description: It is unavailable to get such a bike at this price; it is amazing. The Honda Dio remains a powerhouse in the 110cc scooter segment, successfully blending aggressive, "moto-scooter" aesthetics with the rock-solid reliability that defines the Honda brand. Designed primarily for a younger demographic, its sharp lines, apron-mounted LED headlamp, and sleek bodywork give it a modern, sporty presence that stands out against more conservative commuter models. At its heart lies a refined 110cc PGM-FI engine, which is remarkably smooth and quiet thanks to the ACG silent start system. While it isn’t built for high-speed racing, it provides a punchy and agile performance for city commutes, paired with an impressive fuel efficiency of around 45–50 kmpl. One of the most significant upgrades in recent iterations is the inclusion of telescopic front suspension and a 12-inch front wheel, which have vastly improved its handling over potholes and uneven urban roads. The scooter is also packed with practical features like an external fuel filler cap, which eliminates the hassle of lifting the seat at petrol pumps, and a side-stand engine cut-off for enhanced safety. Despite its many strengths, the Dio’s lightweight fibre body—while excellent for nimbleness and fuel economy—doesn’t feel as rugged as the metal-bodied Activa and can be prone to minor rattles after years of heavy use on rough roads. Additionally, taller riders might find the floorboard space a bit cramped during long rides. However, these are minor trade-offs for a vehicle that offers such a high resale value and low maintenance costs. Ultimately, the Honda Dio is the definitive choice for college students and urban professionals who want a stylish, easy-to-handle, and dependable machine that makes a statement without breaking the bank. It remains a top-tier contender for anyone prioritising flair and agility in their daily ride.

reviews.title: Desert heart. Mountain soul.
reviews.description: This bike is a camel that never gets tired.</br>If endurance had two wheels, it would be the Himalayan 450. This machine is built to go the distance — whether it’s highways, mountains, or city traffic.</br>Pros – What I Love About This Bike</br>Ride Quality – Extremely Comfortable</br>The suspension setup is brilliant. It absorbs bumps effortlessly, making long rides feel easy on the body.</br>Impressive Mileage for a 450cc</br>For a 450cc engine, getting around 28 km/l is very respectable. With this kind of power on tap, the efficiency is more than satisfactory.</br>Eye-Catching Looks</br>The design stands out. People notice when you ride past. It has a strong road presence.</br>Effortless Cruising</br>Cruising at 120–130 km/h feels smooth and stable. The bike doesn’t feel stressed.</br>Strong Service Network</br>Royal Enfield has one of the widest service networks in India, which adds peace of mind for long-distance riders.</br>Affordable Maintenance</br>Regular service costs around ₹1,800, which is quite economical compared to many rivals in this segment.</br>Built for Long Distances</br>Thanks to the soft suspension and effective windscreen, riding 700–800 km in a day is very manageable.</br>Large 17-Litre Fuel Tank</br>With a 17L tank and ~28 km/l mileage, it can comfortably cover 400+ km on a full tank — perfect for remote stretches.</br>Punchy Throttle & Strong Low-End Torque</br>Throttle response feels sharp, especially in the initial pull. Like most Royal Enfield bikes, the low-end torque is strong, which means fewer gear changes in city traffic.</br> Cons – Minor Downsides</br>Slight Vibrations at 80–90 km/h</br>There are mild vibrations in this range. You do get used to them over time, and they don’t take away from the overall experience.</br> Stock Mirrors Could Be Better</br>The stock mirrors aren’t the best and could use an upgrade.</br>My Buying Story</br>I wasn’t always a fan of Royal Enfield.</br>After riding the Royal Enfield Classic 350 to Ladakh, I felt it struggled at high altitudes due to low oxygen levels. Later, I bought the KTM 390 Duke and absolutely loved its performance — super punchy and aligned perfectly with my riding style.</br>Eventually, I wanted an adventure bike and planned to buy the KTM 390 Adventure. I even took a test ride and paid the booking amount.</br>On my way home, I happened to pass by a Royal Enfield showroom and thought, “Let me just take a test ride — I won’t buy it.”</br>Just 5 kilometres later, I was already in love.</br>It felt like sitting on a sofa while the bike moved effortlessly. Compared to the KTM 390 Adventure, I found it significantly more comfortable, and the low-end torque was stronger. In Delhi NCR traffic, I didn’t have to shift gears constantly.</br>I went home, discussed it with my wife, and she took a test ride as a pillion. She found it extremely comfortable too.</br>I cancelled the KTM booking and brought home the Himalayan 450.</br>The first thing I did? Took it straight to Ladakh.</br>Covered nearly 3,500 km — and honestly, I have zero complaints regarding performance or comfort.</br>Final Verdict</br>If you don’t have height-related concerns, this machine will not disappoint you.</br>The Himalayan 450 is built for riders who value comfort, endurance, torque, and real-world usability over aggressive top-end performance.</br>It’s not just a bike.</br>It’s a long-distance companion.</br>A machine that refuses to get tired.

reviews.title: One Bike That Does It All – Touring, Trails & Daily Rides
reviews.description: bought the Royal Enfield Himalayan 450, looking for an all-purpose motorcycle, and it has truly lived up to that expectation. This bike can be used almost anywhere – city rides, highways, long touring journeys, and even off-road trails. The buying experience was smooth, and the bike instantly feels premium and well-built.</br>The riding experience is excellent, especially for touring and adventure riding. The suspension setup is very comfortable and handles bad roads, potholes, and off-road trails with ease. The bike does feel a little heavy initially, especially at low speeds, but once you start riding regularly, you slowly get used to the weight, and it no longer feels like a problem.</br>The engine is aggressive and noticeably more powerful compared to older Himalayans. Power delivery is strong, smooth, and confidence-inspiring, whether you’re overtaking on highways or climbing rough terrain. The bike feels stable at high speeds and planted on long rides. The upright seating position, wide handlebars, and comfortable seat make long-distance touring fatigue-free.</br>In terms of looks, the Himalayan 450 has a rugged and modern adventure-bike design that stands out on the road. Servicing and maintenance so far have been reasonable, and regular servicing keeps the bike smooth and reliable.</br>Pros: Powerful engine, excellent suspension, touring comfort, great off-road capability, all-round usability.</br>Cons: Slightly heavy for beginners, could be intimidating at first.</br>Maintenance Tip: Keep chain lubrication regular, check tyre pressure before long rides, and follow service intervals for the best performance.</br>Overall, the Himalayan 450 is a perfect all-rounder for riders who want one bike for everything.

reviews.title: Royal Enfield GT 650 – Worth the Hype in 2026?
reviews.description: I have been riding the Continental GT 650 for some time now, and my experience with this motorcycle has been excellent overall. It perfectly blends classic café racer styling with modern engineering, making it a great choice for riders who want both performance and strong road presence.</br>Starting with comfort, the riding posture is sporty but manageable. Initially, it may feel slightly aggressive, but once you get used to it, the bike feels comfortable for daily city rides as well as longer weekend trips. The seat quality is decent, and the suspension handles most road conditions well. The bike feels stable and well-balanced, especially while cruising on highways.</br>The 648cc parallel-twin engine is one of the biggest highlights. It is smooth, refined, and delivers power in a very linear manner. Acceleration is strong, and there are minimal vibrations even at higher speeds. Overtaking on highways feels effortless, and the exhaust note adds to the overall riding experience.</br>In terms of mileage, the bike performs quite well for its segment. I am getting around 22–25 km/l, depending on traffic and riding style, which is reasonable for a 650cc motorcycle.</br>After-sales service has also been a positive experience. Service centers are easily accessible, and the staff is professional and supportive. Maintenance costs are not very high, and spare parts or aftermarket accessories are readily available in the market, which makes ownership more convenient.</br>The build quality feels solid and premium. The retro design, twin exhausts, and overall finish give the bike a strong road presence, and it often attracts attention wherever I go.</br>Final Verdict:</br>The Continental GT 650 is a great package for anyone looking for a stylish, powerful, and reliable middleweight motorcycle. It offers a perfect balance of performance, comfort, and value for money, making the overall ownership experience truly satisfying.

reviews.title: Pulsar F250 11 months ownership review
reviews.description: Buying experience - I had to buy a 2 lakh motorcycle after selling (due to back pain issues) my Bullet Electra Twinspark 2014 in December 2022. Apart from F250/N250, I considered motorcycles like the Hornet 2.0, FZ25 & R15S, Xpulse 200T 4v and Apache 200 as options. Didn't consider RS200, NS200 or 220 since they're dated. Test rode all options in Jan 2023 and immediately realized that no other bike in the segment is providing such a plush ride with decent handling. It also fulfilled most of my other requirements as well. Without much delay took a dual channel unit home in Feb 2023 for around 1.75L on-road Thane.</br>Riding experience - After riding a long-stroke RE engine for years, it took me some time to get used to an over-square engine and also to F250's long turning radius. But once you get used to this, this bike becomes fun to ride.</br>Looks - Subjective. I wanted some sort of fairing but not too wide like the RS200.</br>Performance - Power and torque are sufficient for cities and highways. The bike is stable at triple-digit speeds. There are vibes post 100kmph but we rarely get to cruise above 100 on Indian roads. But the vibes are manageable during occasional top-speed runs. Fuel efficiency is very good for a 250cc motorcycles. You can get 33-38 kmpl in the city depending upon road and traffic conditions. On highways, this gives above 40 if you cruise between 70 and 90kmph. Efficiency starts to drop after 90kmph. For instance, if you cruise at 100kmph constantly you'll get around 37-38kmpl. LED projectors are decent too.</br>Servicing and maintenance - My running is not too high, I have got 2 free services done. 1st free service with an oil change cost me around 800 and 2nd service with an oil top-up costs 400. Bajaj's 20W-50 oil by the Gulf is not the best for highways. Gets black at 2000 km. I recommend Motul, Idemitsu or Shell. Overall maintenance of any bike depends upon the rider's riding style.</br>Pros - </br>1. Good power and torque delivery, good suspension.</br>2. Awesome brake bite and feedback from both the brakes in dual channel ABS unit.</br>3. Aerodynamic fairing.</br>4. Good headlight throw.</br>5. A good semi-digital meter console that provides adequate information.</br>6. A combination of a comfortable riding posture, great fuel efficiency and 14-litre tank capacity gives a riding range of more than 500kms on a single tank easily which makes it an efficient tourer.</br>7. Spare parts availability is decent.</br>Cons - </br>1. RVM on the fairing panel vibrates even at slower speeds and lower RPMs (I've installed NS200 RVM on the handlebar).</br>2. Plastic panels are a lot better than before but still need improvement. Stickering peels off too easily.</br>2. Being a good tourer, it must have had a display for maps and navigation.</br>3. Bajaj service centre people aren't good everywhere. I had to change my service centre since the one associated with my dealer didn't even listen to my issues/feedback properly.</br>4. Noticeable vibes under the rider's seat after 7k rpm. But doesn't stop the motorcycle from pulling further as such.</br>Can't recollect any other cons.
reviews.tips: Use better oils than OEM on any vehicle if highway use is more. Be gentle on potholes as being rash can harm the suspension, chassis and your back.

reviews.title: Very good bike according to this price points but it's not perfect
reviews.description: The TVS Apache RR 310 is a motorcycle that tries to strike a rare balance between everyday usability and genuine sport-bike character, and for the most part, it succeeds impressively. At first glance, the design immediately stands out with its sharp fairing, aggressive stance, aerodynamic winglets, and premium paint options, giving it a visual presence that feels closer to bigger superbikes than most 300 cc machines. The build quality is solid and reassuring, with tight panel gaps and a sense that TVS has paid close attention to fit and finish. Powering the bike is a 312.2 cc liquid-cooled single-cylinder engine that produces around 38 PS, and while it may not be the most explosive motor in the segment, it is refined, tractable, and confidence-inspiring, especially for riders who want strong performance without feeling intimidated. The engine shines in the mid-range, making highway overtakes easy, while the top end is engaging enough for spirited riding and occasional track use. One of the RR 310’s biggest strengths is its electronics package, which includes ride-by-wire, multiple riding modes (Urban, Rain, Sport, and Track), a TFT display with Bluetooth connectivity, and safety aids like dual-channel ABS and a slipper clutch, features that are still rare in this category. Handling is another highlight, as the chassis feels stable at high speeds and composed through corners, while the suspension setup is firm but not punishing, making it suitable for Indian road conditions. Despite being a fully faired sport bike, the riding posture is surprisingly manageable, allowing it to be used for daily commuting without excessive wrist or back strain, although the pillion seat and small fuel tank limit its long-distance touring comfort. On the downside, the price can feel slightly high compared to rivals, and hardcore performance enthusiasts may find the power delivery a bit too linear rather than thrilling. However, when you look at the Apache RR 310 as a complete package—combining design, technology, comfort, and performance—it emerges as a well-rounded, mature sport bike that caters not just to speed lovers, but to riders who want a premium, versatile machine that looks exciting, feels safe, and remains practical enough to live with every day.

reviews.title: perfect for daily usage
reviews.description: As an owner, the TVS Apache RR 310 feels like a well-rounded and premium sportbike that balances performance, comfort, and everyday usability. The engine is smooth and refined, making it easy to ride in city traffic while still being stable and confident on highways at 110–120 km/h. Handling is one of its biggest strengths—the bike feels planted in corners and very stable at high speeds, supported by strong brakes and good suspension tuning. The design still turns heads and looks much more expensive than it is, though the low ground clearance and engine heat in slow traffic can be minor drawbacks. Overall, the RR 310 is ideal for riders who want a stylish, comfortable, and confidence-inspiring fully-faired motorcycle rather than an all-out aggressive machine

reviews.title: A Perfect Mix of Design, Comfort, and Daily Performance
reviews.description: I’ve been riding the TVS Apache RR 310 for a while now, and honestly, it feels like a complete package. The first thing that stands out is the design. The bike looks premium from every angle and still turns heads on the road. The riding posture is sporty but not uncomfortable, which makes it usable for both city rides and longer highway runs. Performance-wise, the engine feels smooth and refined, with enough power for confident overtakes and stable cruising. Handling is sharp, and the bike feels planted even at higher speeds. Brakes inspire confidence, and suspension setup handles bad roads better than expected for a sport bike. Servicing experience has been decent so far, and maintenance hasn’t been a headache. Overall, the RR 310 feels well-built, balanced, and thoughtfully designed. If you want a sport bike that looks great, performs well, and is practical for real-world riding, this bike makes a lot of sense.

reviews.title: Bestest mileage king
reviews.description: If you're looking for a bike that turns every drop of fuel into a journey, look no further than the TVS Sport ES+. After months of riding, I can confidently say this machine lives up to its legendary reputation, delivering not just exceptional performance, but an economy that simply sets it apart in the commuter segment. It's more than just a bike; it's a reliable partner for daily life, designed to keep your focus on the destination, not the fuel gauge.</br>​The biggest star of the show is, without a doubt, the mileage. The ET-Fi (EcoThrust Fuel injection) technology is a marvel. I have been consistently getting outstanding fuel efficiency, which translates directly into significant savings. For anyone with a substantial daily commute, the TVS Sport ES+ offers a financial relief that few other bikes can match. This incredible economy, combined with the bike's low maintenance, makes the ownership experience stress-free and pocket-friendly.</br>​Beyond the numbers, the ride quality is impressive for a bike in this class. The ES+ (Electric Start) is a game-changer for quick, hassle-free starts in city traffic, adding a touch of modern convenience. The seating is plush and comfortable, perfectly suited for long hours in the saddle, whether navigating pothole-ridden lanes or smooth highways. The synchronized braking system (SBS) adds a crucial layer of safety, making me feel secure during sudden stops. The suspension setup, while simple, is tuned well to absorb the bumps and undulations of typical Indian roads, ensuring a smooth and fatigue-free ride.</br>​The aesthetics of the TVS Sport ES+ are sharp and purposeful. It’s styled conservatively but smartly, with attractive decals and a robust, no-nonsense stance. It looks durable because it is durable—the build quality is solid, and the fit and finish are excellent. The long-lasting paint and durable components assure me that this bike is built to handle the rigors of time.</br>​In summary, the TVS Sport ES+ is the ultimate champion for the everyday commuter. It blends unmatched fuel efficiency with solid reliability, modern convenience via the electric start, and a comfortable ride. It’s a bike that is easy on the wallet, easy to maintain, and a pleasure to ride daily. If your priority is maximum savings and maximum dependability, the TVS Sport ES+ is an absolute winner.

reviews.title: First Impression Of The Duke 390
reviews.description: Don't own the Duke 390 but I have spent enough time riding and experiencing it through test rides and friends bikes to form a clear opinion. From the first moment I saw it in person the bike looked sharp and aggressive. The design is bold and modern and it definitely grabs attention on the road. When I finally rode it the posture felt upright and comfortable but still sporty which I really liked</br>The engine is the most exciting part of this bike. Even on a short ride you can feel how powerful and responsive it is. The throttle response is quick and the bike accelerates very fast almost too fast for beginners in my opinion. It feels like the bike always wants to go faster and that makes riding it thrilling. Since it comes from KTM the performance focused nature makes complete sense</br>What impressed me a lot was the handling. The Duke 390 feels very light and easy to control. Taking turns and corners felt natural and confidence boosting even though I was not pushing it too hard. The chassis feels stable and planted. However the suspension felt quite stiff on rough roads. You really feel the bumps and broken patches which might not be ideal for daily bad roads</br>Braking performance is strong and reassuring. The ABS works well and gives confidence especially for someone who is just testing the bike and not fully used to its power. The instrument cluster looks modern and gives all the necessary information clearly</br>Overall my experience with the Duke 390 was very positive. It feels like a bike made for riders who enjoy excitement and sharp performance. It may not be the most comfortable or forgiving bike but it surely leaves a strong impression and makes you want to ride it again and again.

reviews.title: Best Product
reviews.description: KTM Duke 390 ek aisi naked sports bike hai jo performance, design aur advanced technology ka zabardast combination offer karti hai, aur jo riders ko sirf ek bike nahi balki ek pure riding experience deti hai. Is bike me 398.7cc ka powerful single-cylinder, liquid-cooled engine milta hai jo lagbhag 46 PS ki power aur 39 Nm ka torque generate karta hai, jiske wajah se city me smooth riding aur highway par aggressive performance dono ka maza milta hai. Duke 390 ka throttle response kaafi sharp hai aur acceleration itna strong hai ki 0 se 100 km/h ki speed bahut jaldi achieve ho jati hai, jo is segment me isse kaafi special banata hai. Design ki baat karein to iska streetfighter look instantly attention grab karta hai, jisme sharp tank shrouds, muscular fuel tank aur split LED headlamp is bike ko ek bold aur premium feel dete hain. KTM Duke 390 sirf looks aur power tak limited nahi hai, balki features ke mamle me bhi yeh bike kaafi aage hai, kyunki isme full-colour TFT display milta hai jo Bluetooth connectivity ke saath navigation, call alerts aur music control jaise modern features support karta hai. Safety aur control ke liye bike me ride-by-wire system, multiple riding modes jaise Street, Rain aur Track, cornering ABS aur traction control jaise advanced electronics diye gaye hain, jo har tarah ki road conditions me rider ko confidence dete hain. Suspension setup me WP USD front forks aur rear monoshock Indian roads par kaafi achha kaam karte hain aur corners me bike ko stable aur precise banate hain, jabki braking system me front aur rear disc brakes ke saath dual-channel ABS strong aur reliable stopping power provide karta hai. Mileage ki baat karein to Duke 390 lagbhag 25 se 28 km/l ka average deti hai, jo is performance level ki bike ke liye reasonable maana jata hai, haan maintenance thoda mehnga ho sakta hai lekin jo riders performance aur thrill ko priority dete hain unke liye yeh compromise bilkul worth it hai. Overall, KTM Duke 390 un logon ke liye ek perfect choice hai jo ek powerful, feature-loaded aur exciting naked sports bike chahte hain jo har ride ko yaadgar bana de.

reviews.title: 39T Beast Rider Must Know
reviews.description: Certainly! Here’s a detailed overview of the KTM RC 390, covering various aspects of the motorcycle:</br>1. Buying Experience</br>The KTM RC 390 is generally available through KTM dealerships. The buying experience often includes a test ride, which is a good opportunity to get a feel for the bike before purchasing. Dealerships typically offer various financing options and promotions. The RC 390 is positioned as a premium sports bike in the entry-level category, so expect a higher price compared to other entry-level models. The purchase process usually involves choosing between standard and optional features, such as additional accessories or extended warranties.</br>2. Riding Experience</br>The RC 390 is known for its sporty and agile riding experience. It has a light and nimble feel, making it well-suited for both city commuting and spirited weekend rides. The bike features a responsive throttle, strong brakes, and a well-tuned suspension that provides confidence in corners and on straights. Its aerodynamic design and comfortable ergonomics cater to both track days and everyday use, though the aggressive riding position may not be ideal for long-distance touring.</br>3. Details About Looks and Performance</br>Looks: The RC 390 sports a sharp, aggressive design with a distinctive front fairing and aerodynamic bodywork. Its sleek, race-inspired styling includes a high-mounted exhaust and LED lighting, giving it a modern, high-tech appearance.</br>Performance: Powered by a 373cc single-cylinder, liquid-cooled engine, the RC 390 produces around 44 horsepower and 37 Nm of torque. This engine is known for its lively performance and smooth power delivery. The bike features a six-speed gearbox and offers quick acceleration and a top speed that is impressive for its class. The suspension setup includes a WP front fork and rear mono-shock, which provides a good balance between handling and comfort.</br>4. Servicing and Maintenance</br>The RC 390 requires regular servicing to maintain its performance and longevity. Routine maintenance includes oil changes, filter replacements, and checks on brake pads and tires. KTM dealerships and authorized service centers are equipped to handle these tasks. Parts and services are generally available, but costs can be higher compared to more mainstream brands. Regular maintenance is crucial to ensure the bike performs optimally and to prevent potential issues.</br>5. Pros and Cons</br>Pros:</br>Performance: Strong engine performance and agile handling make it a joy to ride.</br>Design: Eye-catching and aerodynamic styling that stands out.</br>Technology: Features like a full-color TFT display and advanced electronics (e.g., ride-by-wire, traction control) enhance the riding experience.</br>Cons:</br>Comfort: Aggressive riding position may not be comfortable for long rides or commuting.</br>Price: Higher price point compared to other entry-level sports bikes.</br>Maintenance Costs: Service and parts can be more expensive compared to some other brands in the same category.</br>Overall, the KTM RC 390 is a great choice for riders looking for a sporty, well-designed motorcycle with strong performance, though it might not be the most practical option for everyday commuting or long-distance touring.
reviews.tips:
Regular Oil Changes: Change the engine oil and filter every 5,000 km (3,100 miles) to ensure smooth engine operation.
Check Fluid Levels: Regularly check and top up coolant and brake fluid levels.
Inspect Tires: Monitor tire pressure and tread depth. Properly inflated and well-maintained tires improve safety and performance.
Brake Maintenance: Check brake pads for wear and replace them as needed to maintain effective braking.
Clean and Lubricate Chain: Keep the chain clean and lubricated, and check its tension regularly.
Battery Care: Ensure the battery is charged and connections are clean to avoid starting issues.
Scheduled Service: Follow the manufacturer’s recommended service intervals and use authorized service centers for major maintenance.

reviews.title: Choose Gixxer Over R15
reviews.description: I’ve been riding the Suzuki Gixxer 150 SF for the past two years, and it’s been an absolute joy. The bike delivers a perfect balance of performance and practicality for daily commuting and weekend rides. Its 155cc engine feels smooth and responsive, with good low-end torque that makes city traffic easy to navigate and enough punch for highway stretches. The handling is confidence-inspiring with a stable chassis and precise feedback, which makes cornering fun yet safe. The semi-faired design not only enhances the sporty look but also offers decent wind protection on longer rides. Fuel efficiency has been impressive, averaging around 45-50 km/l in mixed conditions, which is great for daily use. Comfort is good for both the rider and pillion; seats are well-cushioned and riding posture feels natural even after long hours. Maintenance costs have been reasonable, and Suzuki’s reliability has shown in trouble-free ownership so far. Overall, for any rider who wants a reliable, stylish, and fun 150cc bike, the Gixxer 150 SF is worth considering.

reviews.title: Suzuki Gixxer sf is perfect bike in 150cc segment.
reviews.description: The ride is very comfortable on long and city rides. The sitting portion is very nice. Mileage of the bike is around 45 km/l, which is enough in the 150cc segment. Braking is perfect, and ABS works perfectly, and the pickup of the bike is quick. The most balanced bike in this segment. The sporty look of the bike is awesome. Shocker and suspension of the bike are perfect. Ground clearance is perfect.

reviews.title: Suzuki Gixxer SF 150 Sporty Looks with Everyday Comfort
reviews.description: The Suzuki Gixxer SF 150 is a great choice for riders who want a stylish, fully-faired motorcycle without compromising on daily usability. Its sharp design, inspired by bigger superbikes, still turns heads on the road and gives a premium feel in the 150cc segment.</br>The 155cc air-cooled engine is smooth and refined, making city riding easy and stress-free. Power delivery is linear, so the bike doesn’t feel aggressive but remains very predictable, which is ideal for daily commuting. On highways, it can comfortably cruise around 90–100 km/h, though it’s not meant for hardcore racing or high-speed thrills.</br>Handling is one of the strong points of the Gixxer SF. The bike feels stable at higher speeds and corners confidently, while the suspension setup balances comfort and control well. Braking is reliable with single-channel ABS, offering good safety for everyday riding.</br>In terms of comfort, the riding posture is slightly sporty but not extreme. This makes it suitable for long rides as well as daily office commutes. Mileage is decent for a faired bike, making it pocket-friendly in the long run.</br>Overall, the Suzuki Gixxer SF 150 is perfect for riders who want a combination of sporty design, comfort, reliability, and low maintenance. It may not be the fastest in its class, but it excels as a stylish and practical all-rounder motorcycle.

reviews.title: Suzuki Gixxer – Built to Rule the Streets
reviews.description: The Suzuki Gixxer is a stylish and reliable street motorcycle that offers a perfect balance of performance, comfort, and mileage. Its muscular design, sharp tank extensions, and sporty stance give it a premium look in the 150cc segment. The build quality feels solid, and the fit and finish are impressive for the price.</br>The engine is smooth and refined, delivering strong mid-range performance, which makes city riding effortless and enjoyable. Gear shifts are slick, vibrations are minimal, and the bike feels stable even at higher speeds. The handling is confident, thanks to its well-tuned suspension and wide tyres, making corners fun and predictable.</br>Comfort is another strong point of the Gixxer. The riding posture is upright and relaxed, suitable for daily commuting as well as short highway rides. The seat is comfortable for both rider and pillion, and the braking performance is reliable with good stopping power.</br>Overall, the Suzuki Gixxer is a great choice for riders who want a sporty-looking bike that’s practical, easy to maintain, and dependable for everyday use. It’s especially ideal for those looking for a refined engine, good handling, and long-term reliability.

reviews.title: Great Sport Tourer and City Friendly

Suspension works absolutely brilliantly. I've done 2 rides with a pillion on highway and some bad roads and they were mostly comfortable if we compare on the suspension end keeping put the pillion seat's comfort. Mileage is also good. The max I got is 46kmpl on the highway. In city I constantly get 38 to 40kmpl but that's because I like to ride aggressively some times lol. It will give much better mileage if ridden smoothly. Hope my review helps others.

More importantly, is it worth the premium over its rivals in the quarter-litre space? We rode the motorcycle for this comprehensive review and to find answers to those questions.

reviews.title: Gixxer 250 - Long term review
reviews.description: Basically, I've been riding this bike for around 5 years ( 30000kms), it is one of the finest 200-plus machines that I've had ( including Duke and fz25 & cbr 250 that I've had in the past). </br>The bike is given the same mileage for the last 3 years, however, it gives close to 35kmpl on highways. It provides wonderful stability while cornering or riding at high speeds. The riding seat is pretty comfortable but the pillion seat is not. </br>Pros- cost efficient </br>Value for money. </br>Low cost & super reliable parts. </br>Extraordinary after-sales service. </br>Wonderful engine, lovable brakes( both front & rear). </br>Finest rear suspension. </br>Cons- design not upto the mark. </br>Waiting time for parts. </br>The front suspension could've been a bit better with usd forks. </br>That's it, I hope it helps people who are riding the bike or looking to buy a reliable, powerful 250cc.

You can use it for long rides. Good suspensions.</br>Cons:- you feel the weight on your wrist. Low mileage. No kick. no choke button. No double stand.</br>Overall if you're looking for a sporty bike around 2 lakh then this is for you

reviews.title: It will do it all but can you?
reviews.description: This is a great all rounder for someone starting out and they do not want anything too intimidating , too flashy or in the face with the design or the tech on offer. This flows under the radar with it's simple design, and somber colours on choice. I've clocked over 48K on the odo covering almost all of uttarakahnd, Amritsar, Indore, Jaipur and many other places on this. I've toured alone with luggage and  with a pillion + luggage setup as well. This motorcycle  performs flawless in any weather conditions and with basic maintenance and some useful mods  like Fog lamps, tail rack, you can greatly increase the usability of the bike. Sure it's not as powerful or tech laden  the counterparts, but it's exactly where it shines. It's the Basics done right! It's a delightful riding experience that helps you hone your skill as a motorcyclist and Suzuki has done an amazing job with the tractability of the engine. The bike has never run hot even in the scorching heat of  M.P upwards of 47 degrees ( I was travelling from Delhi to Indore).  It could use a facelift  upgrading to better quality forks and a bigger fuel tank for an increased range, the stock heaadlight unit can be improved by a lot and the aftermarket for it's accessories is a questionable. You'll have to search around a lot if you want something specific to be done but overall it's a  great beginner friendly machine  for someone just starting out wanting something simple and no nonsense not attracting too much attention or looking for a secondary motorcycle to do the daily runs while being easy on the pocket. </br>Pros- </br>-Bare minimum tech, less things to go wrong</br>- Legendary reliability, and easy on the pocket even for students</br>- A great way of approaching  and overcoming the learning curve</br>- Simple design, minimum to no graphic stickering</br>- Good FE</br>- Good Cruiser for highways and Office runs</br>- A simple, fun ,riding machine guaranteed to give you a huge smile on your face</br>- Good corner carver, Pegs can seem to scrape but that's all right</br>- rock stable even at 120+, inspiring confidence</br>Cons- </br>- Pricing is a big factor when considering this motorcycle, I feel Suzuki could give a bit more equipment like - </br>  - better forks ( After clocking 48k on the odo, I wish This bike had bigger and better quality forks for my highway duties) </br>  - a stronger headlight unit ( I fixed it by installing aftermarket foglamps)</br>- LED turn indicators ( swapped the bulbs for LED units in the existing assembly)</br>- Bit more info on the speedo like distance to empty or AVG FE ( although I'm good at math but I' m human too)</br>- Aftersales support and servicing still needs a huge improvement and also what deters buyers from considering it ( a constant headache as mechanics are not well trained )</br>- With the new emission norms, fuel tank needs to be increased to 13-14 L compared to the existing 12. ( range is on par with the other motorcycles of this class, but can be improved upon).</br>Except for a few niggles, this an absolutely fantastic piece of engineering and I would gladly recommend anyone willing to live with a few trade offs and who wants a genuine riding experience with not too much drama, this bike will do it all and will take a beating as well. At the end of the day you decide what you will do with the motorcycle and how it makes you feel. </br>Cheers, happy riding folks :)
reviews.tips: Please clean and Lube your chain every 10-15 days if you ride an average of 25-30 kms a day. Can upgrade the seat cusions for more comfort. Pay attention to the handlebar and cone set, Suzukis have had the issue with their grease so when getting your cone set greased or replaced,  get a castrol or a good wax to use for the application as the one they use gets hard after sometime and you will repeatedly face the issue of your handlebar being too tight. Pay close attention to the handle T and get it inspected every year if you feel your front of the bike not behaving as intended.  Clutch cables , break fluids need to be changed as per usage and always be checked for wear and tear. Keep your paperwork watertight ass you might need to call up the Suzuki helpline for servicing issues. You take care of it, it will take care of you.

reviews.title: Japanese Beast
reviews.description: One of the most exciting experiences of my life was riding a Suzuki Hayabusa, one of the fastest and most iconic superbikes in the world. I had always admired this bike in pictures and videos, but riding it in real life was a completely different feeling.</br>The day I got the opportunity, I felt both excited and nervous. The Hayabusa looked powerful and elegant with its aerodynamic design and massive body. When I first sat on the bike, I could feel the strength of the machine beneath me. The riding position was slightly aggressive, which made me feel like a professional racer.</br>When I started the engine, the deep roar of the powerful engine immediately gave me goosebumps. It was not just a sound; it felt like the heartbeat of a beast ready to run. As I slowly released the clutch and accelerated, the bike moved smoothly and effortlessly.</br>Once I reached an open road, I gently twisted the throttle. The acceleration was unbelievably fast. Within seconds, the bike picked up speed so quickly that I could feel the wind rushing against my body. Despite the high speed, the bike felt extremely stable and well-balanced. The handling was smooth, and every movement of the throttle responded instantly.</br>What impressed me the most was the control and comfort of the bike. Even though it is known for its speed, the Hayabusa felt very stable and safe when ridden carefully. The advanced braking system and strong suspension made the ride feel secure.</br>The entire experience filled me with adrenaline and joy. Riding the Hayabusa made me understand why it is called a legendary superbike. It was not just about speed; it was about power, precision, and the thrill of riding such an incredible machine.</br>This experience will always remain one of the most memorable moments of my life. It taught me that riding powerful bikes requires responsibility, skill, and respect for the machine.

reviews.title: Hayabusa is the real king of roads
reviews.description: Hayabusa isn't a bike, Hayabusa is a feeling. As soon as you twist the throttle, it’s like you experience pure power coupled with unstoppable smoothness. Hayabusa handles the roads like a breeze, no matter how big the engine size is. The presence on the roads is unmatched—heads turn around wherever the bike goes. For me, Hayabusa isn't about competing with other bikes, it’s about feeling the controlled power, long rides, and owning a legend.

reviews.title: The Suzuki Hayabusa Review: Speed, Soul, and the Ultimate Hyperbike Experience
reviews.description: The Suzuki Hayabusa stands as the definitive icon of the hyper-sport motorcycle class, blending a potent 1,340cc inline-four engine—producing 190 bhp and a substantial 150 Nm of torque—with its legendary, wind-cheating aerodynamic design to achieve blistering, electronically limited top speeds of around 300 km/h. The latest generation refines this power with a comprehensive suite of advanced electronics known as the Suzuki Intelligent Ride System (S.I.R.S.), which includes lean-angle-sensitive traction control, cornering ABS, and a bi-directional quickshifter managed by an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), ensuring that its immense performance remains both manageable and safe. The riding experience is characterized by effortless, linear acceleration and unshakeable stability at high speeds. Despite its 266 kg weight, which provides a planted feel on the highway, the Hayabusa offers a surprisingly comfortable, relaxed ergonomic riding position suitable for long-distance touring. The bike’s build quality, fit, and finish are premium, retaining that unmistakable, muscular "Busa" look. Ultimately, the Hayabusa is more than just transportation; it is an engineering masterpiece—a perfect blend of raw power, cutting-edge technology, comfort, and timeless style that delivers an addictive, smooth rush of speed and earns a stellar 9.8/10 rating as "the ultimate ride" for those who crave speed with soul.

reviews.title: fantastic experience

The throttle response is incredibly smooth, and the acceleration remains unmatched in its class — a true adrenaline rush every time you twist the wrist.</br>Handling is another area where the Hayabusa surprises. The advanced electronics package — including ride modes, traction control, quick shifter, and cornering ABS — gives riders both confidence and safety without compromising on thrill.</br>Comfort-wise, it’s excellent for long rides with an ergonomic seating position and a beautifully tuned suspension system. The build quality, fit, and finish are premium, while the design retains that legendary “Busa” look — muscular, aggressive, and unmistakably Suzuki. The Suzuki Hayabusa is a masterpiece — a perfect blend of power, technology, comfort, and timeless style. It’s not just a bike; it’s an emotion for every superbike enthusiast.</br>⭐ Rating: 9.8/10</br>🏍️ Verdict: “For those who crave speed with soul — the Hayabusa remains the ultimate ride.”

reviews.title: Premium Motorrad experience on a budget
reviews.description: Firstly, this is the prettiest bike in the sub 4 lakh range. Period. And the BMW badge and design language is the cherry on top.</br>I was sold right from the point I entered the dealership for the first time. Before I even get to the bike, I have to say no other brand compares to BMW in terms of service experience. Yes, you are paying a premium for that, but it is worth it to me. I believe you do not just buy a bike. You buy a brand.</br>As for the bike, I fell in love with the G310R on my very first test drive. There is a very nice grunt to it and the sound builds up in a thrilling way as you climb the RPMs. I have pushed it to the limits ever since buying and loved every second of my ride. After 5000 RPM, the engine note changes into a powerful roar which I cannot describe in words. The 310cc engine pulls really fast, power increases linearly and the lightness of the bike makes it a breeze to flick around. Handling is very easy especially in Bangalore's traffic. And yes, I have had bystanders stare at my bike and one of them asked me the price tag. That alone is worth the 3.7 lakh on-road price for me.</br>There are no free services. This is BMW after all. The first service is at 1 month/1000km, then 12 months/10000km after that. First service cost me around 6-7k. While that may seem high, keep in mind that you only pay once a year. Some other brands have each service cheaper but they have multiple services in a year, so ultimately you're not really paying more here.</br>The only gripe I have with the bike is the gearbox. It is honestly a little clunky at times. Sometimes the gear change doesn't register and you have to consciously push it with your toe harder. Also, the display while sufficient in terms of clarity and information looks dated compared to the coloured TFTs in other bikes in this range.</br>Apart from these shortcomings, I really have no complaints. It has been 9 months since I bought this bike and I am still excited to ride it everytime. If you are only looking for value for money, I would not recommend this bike. But if you value the brand value of a BMW, its unique design and a premium service experience (my first service was completed smoothly in half a day and the staff are very friendly), do not think twice about going for the G 310R. Happy riding!

reviews.title: Go for this motorcycle its worth every penny
reviews.description: The best bike of BMW in this price segment </br>JUST GO FOR IT!!!!</br>2023 BMW G 310 GS Review | Cycle WorldThe BMW G 310 GS is a capable, if somewhat flawed, entry-level adventure tourer that offers the brand's styling and a comfortable riding position, but is held back by a clunky gearbox and rough ride quality over harsh roads. While it handles minor bumps well and has good mid-range torque for city riding and touring, its soft suspension bottoms out on large potholes, and the fly screen offers limited wind protection at higher speeds. The bike's high price and limited off-road performance for its GS designation are notable drawbacks, though its comfortable seat and overall build quality are praised, making it a good daily companion for those aspiring to the GS experience.  </br>Pros:</br>Comfortable Ergonomics: The G 310 GS provides a wide handlebar, accommodating seat, and accommodating footpeg placement, ideal for long-distance touring and comfortable for riders of various sizes. </br>Mid-range Torque: The engine offers good mid-range power, making it suitable for city riding and providing confidence during everyday commutes. </br>Good Build Quality: The bike features excellent fit and finish and high-quality components, consistent with BMW's premium image. </br>Capable on Smooth Roads: It handles minor road imperfections with ease and feels light and agile, making it enjoyable on well-paved roads. </br>Cons:</br>Clunky Gearbox: A common complaint is the gearbox, which can be stiff, leading to missed shifts or difficult gear changes. </br>Vibrations and Noise: Vibrations can be felt at higher speeds, particularly on the handlebars, and the exhaust note isn't always considered soothing. </br>Soft Suspension: The suspension, especially the front forks, can be soft, leading to bottoming out over larger potholes and a bouncy ride on rougher roads. </br>Limited Off-Road Ability: Despite the GS moniker, the bike's limited off-road capability, particularly with the soft suspension, means it's more suited to light trails than serious adventure riding. </br>Premium Price: The bike's high price tag, especially given its components manufactured in India by TVS, is often seen as a significant drawback, according to Quora users. </br>Dated Display: The digital instrument cluster, while informative, lacks the modern flair of the full-color TFT panels found on other bikes.

reviews.title: Feel the difference
reviews.description: This bike is amazing and you can feel it while riding. Look, if you’re hunting for a bike that’s basically a rocket ship with handlebars, the Kawasaki Z900 is your best bet. It’s got that legendary 948cc inline-four that screams like a banshee when you pin it, but it’s actually super chill to ride around town without being a jerky mess. Kawasaki nailed that "Sugomi" look—it basically looks like a crouched predator ready to pounce, and the new TFT screen and quickshifter mean you’re getting all the modern tech goodies without the crazy European price tag. Yeah, it’s a bit of a "heavy boi" compared to some light-weight triples, and the stock seat feels a bit like a wooden plank after an hour, but for the sheer "smile-per-mile" factor, this thing is an absolute weapon. It’s the kind of bike that makes you look back at it every time you park—pure mechanical muscle that doesn't need to try too hard to be the coolest kid on the block.

reviews.title: VERYYY GUUDD I LOVE KAWASEXYY
reviews.description: The Kawasaki Z900 is a powerful middleweight naked motorcycle that blends performance, technology, and everyday usability. It features a 948 cc inline-four engine producing about 123 bhp and 98 Nm of torque, offering smooth yet thrilling acceleration. The bike feels stable and confident thanks to its trellis frame, upside-down front forks, and rear monoshock.</br>The 2025 Z900 adds modern tech such as a 5-inch TFT display, Bluetooth, ride-by-wire throttle, cornering ABS, traction control, ride modes, cruise control, and a bi-directional quick-shifter, making it one of the most feature-rich bikes in its class.</br>Design-wise, it follows Kawasaki’s aggressive “Sugomi” styling, with sharp lines and a muscular stance. The ergonomics strike a balance between sporty and comfortable, suitable for both daily rides and weekend trips, though long rides may feel a bit firm.</br>In practical use, the Z900 delivers about 16–19 km/l, with strong mid-range performance but noticeable heat in city traffic. Maintenance costs are higher than average due to its large engine and premium parts.</br>At around ₹9.52 lakh (ex-showroom India), it competes with the Triumph Street Triple R, Ducati Monster, and Honda CB650R. Riders praise its smooth engine, exciting performance, and value for money, though some note issues like heat, rear-brake feel, and running costs.</br>Pros: Powerful engine, refined handling, rich features, bold design.</br>Cons: High maintenance, heat in traffic, not ideal for beginners.</br>Verdict:</br>The Kawasaki Z900 is a thrilling, feature-packed naked sportbike ideal for experienced riders seeking power and style. It’s less suited for daily city commutes but nearly perfect for weekend rides, highway blasts, and those who want superbike performance without a full-fairing motorcycle.

reviews.title: About z900
reviews.description: The Kawasaki Z900 truly excels by delivering a thrilling, pure motorcycling experience centered around its brilliant 948cc inline-four engine. This heart of the beast is renowned for its smooth, manageable power delivery at low and mid-range RPMs, making it surprisingly tractable in city traffic, yet it effortlessly transforms into a high-revving, intoxicating rush of acceleration as you push into the upper rev range. Paired with its aggressive, 'Sugomi' streetfighter styling and a distinctive, factory-tuned exhaust note, the Z900 offers a compelling blend of brute force and everyday usability that is hard to match in its class.</br>​Beyond the exceptional performance, the Z900 earns high marks for its superb overall value proposition. It backs up its power with modern electronic aids, including Traction Control (KTRC), multiple Riding Modes (Sport, Road, Rain), and a clear TFT color display with smartphone connectivity. </br>Overall i love this bike

reviews.title: An Honest Statement
reviews.description: I never imagined that I would be learning to ride a motorcycle in my 40s. Most people pick up biking in their teens or twenties, but for me, it happened much later. And honestly, the Jawa Perak made that leap less intimidating and a lot more thrilling.</br>The first thing people notice about the Perak is its looks. The matte black bobber styling, the single floating seat, and the clean, minimalist stance—it’s not just a motorcycle, it’s a conversation starter. On the streets of Jammu, it gets attention wherever it goes. People turn their heads, sometimes walk over, and ask questions. It feels good, not because of vanity, but because the bike truly stands apart.</br>The engine is responsive and torquey, yet not overwhelming for someone who started riding later. It gives me confidence on highways and keeps me comfortable in city traffic. The riding posture is different—laid-back, slightly stretched—but once you settle into it, the experience is addictive. The bike feels planted and surefooted on Jammu’s mix of roads.</br>Maintenance and service so far have been fair. Jawa’s network isn’t the widest here, but I’ve found the support polite and helpful. The Perak itself doesn’t demand constant pampering. Stick to the schedule, keep an eye on the basics, and it will serve you well.</br>But what makes this bike truly special for me is how it has changed my perspective on riding. At this age, I’m not chasing speed or showing off—I’m chasing freedom. The Perak delivers that beautifully. Each ride reminds me that it’s never too late to embrace the thrill of the road. For me, the Jawa Perak is more than a motorcycle—it’s proof that biking has no age limit, and the road always has space for those willing to ride. </br>My little words of advice : Always gear up, ride for joy and not for ego, respect the machine, and cherish the journey.

reviews.title: Jawa Perak Standard
reviews.description: The Jawa Perak is one of the most unique and stylish motorcycles in the Indian market, known for its bold design and bobber-style aesthetics. It stands out with its distinctive look, making it a true head-turner on the road. Unlike most conventional bikes, the Perak features a low-slung stance, single-seat setup, and a floating seat design, giving it a retro yet modern appeal.</br>Under the hood, the Jawa Perak is powered by a 334cc, liquid-cooled, single-cylinder engine that produces around 30 bhp and 32.7 Nm of torque. This powerful motor is paired with a 6-speed gearbox, offering smooth gear shifts and a strong mid-range performance. Riders often appreciate the refined engine and the bike’s ability to cruise comfortably at higher speeds, making it suitable for both city rides and highway journeys.</br>The bike’s dual-channel ABS ensures safety and stability, especially while braking on uneven surfaces. Its telescopic front forks and monoshock rear suspension provide a comfortable and controlled ride, absorbing bumps and potholes with ease. With a disc brake setup on both ends, the Perak delivers reliable stopping power.</br>Aesthetically, the Perak is a class apart. It comes with an all-black theme, matte finish, and minimalistic design, making it look elegant yet aggressive. The 18-inch front wheel and 17-inch rear wheel complement its stance, while the fat tires add to its road presence. The floating single seat adds character and enhances the bobber styling, something rarely seen in this price range.</br>What makes the Jawa Perak a good bike is not just its looks but also the overall balance of power, performance, and comfort. It appeals to riders who want individuality and style without compromising on ride quality. Priced competitively, the Perak offers a premium biking experience at an accessible cost, making it a value-for-money choice.</br>In conclusion, the Jawa Perak is more than just a motorcycle—it’s a statement. With its strong engine, advanced features, and iconic design, it blends performance and personality seamlessly, proving to be an excellent option for riders seeking something distinctive and reliable.

reviews.description: The Jawa 42 Bobber is a stylish cruiser motorcycle known for its unique bobber design, low stance, and strong road presence. The bike is popular among riders who like retro-modern styling and mostly ride solo, as it features a floating single seat and minimalist body design. It delivers a mileage of about 25 km/l and has a 12.5 L fuel tank. However, the bike may feel less comfortable for long rides due to its stiff suspension and single-seat setup, and its low ground clearance can be challenging on rough roads or speed breakers. Overall, the Jawa 42 Bobber is a great choice for riders who prioritise style, performance, and a distinctive cruiser look rather than everyday practicality.
