reviews.title: My first bike expeience
reviews.description: The Jawa 42 Bobber is a "heart over head" purchase. If you’re looking for a motorcycle that turns every head on the street, this factory-custom machine is in a league of its own. Looks & Buying The aesthetic is the biggest draw. With its low-slung stance, floating single seat, and bar-end mirrors, it looks like a custom project right off the showroom floor. Buying is straightforward at Jawa-Yezdi dealerships, but be prepared for a "solo" life—there is no pillion option. Riding & Performance Powered by a 334cc liquid-cooled engine , the performance is punchy. It’s a "peaky" motor that loves to be revved, offering great mid-range torque for city overtakes. However, the riding experience is marred by stiff rear suspension and noticeable vibrations once you cross 80–90 km/h. Its low $740\text{mm}$ seat height makes it very accessible, but the low ground clearance means you’ll scrape speed breakers if not careful. Service & Maintenance The service experience is a mixed bag. While the $6,000\km service interval is generous, spare parts availability can be a headache, with owners often reporting long wait times. Service costs are moderate, usually ranging from ₹2,000 to ₹3,500 per visit. The Breakdown Pros: Stunning retro-modern design, addictive exhaust note, slipper clutch, and great road presence. Cons: Stiff ride quality, engine heating in heavy traffic, lack of practicality (zero luggage space), and vibrations at high revs .Maintenance Tips for Owners Engine Oil: Though the manual says $6,000, change your oil every $3,000km for a smoother, cooler engine. Chain Care: The exposed chain attracts grime; clean and lube it every $500\km to avoid premature sprocket wear. Heat Management: Avoid applying PPF or wraps on the tank until after the first two services, as the initial engine heat can cause the adhesive to bubble .Rust Prevention: Use an anti-rust spray on the chrome and exposed bolts during monsoons, as Jawas are prone to surface spotting.

reviews.title: Very good bike and affordable

The seating posture is upright and comfortable, and the handlebar position feels natural. Even during heavy traffic, it’s simple to manage. It’s light enough to move through tight gaps, yet stable enough when cruising around 50 to 60 km/h. I never feel nervous riding it in city conditions.</br>The engine feels smooth and refined. reviews.title: The 10-Years Reality Check of My Activa-125
reviews.description: Ten Years with the Honda Activa 125, </br>After a full decade of daily commutes, grocery runs, and the occasional unplanned monsoon expedition, I’ve realized this isn't just a scooter—it’s essentially a family member that refuses to retire. </br>Strong Body & Build till now, while modern scooters often feel like fragile plastic toys, this machine has a reassuring heft. It has survived parking lot bumps and minor scrapes. Aside from some inevitable rust spots near the floorboard, the structural integrity is still rock solid.</br>You’d expect a ten-year-old engine to feel sluggish, but the initial power is still surprisingly crisp.</br> Low-end Torque: Excellent for navigating bumper-to-bumper city crawls.</br>Reliability: The engine still starts on the first or second thumb-press, provided I don’t skip the oil changes. It’s a testament to Honda’s refined engineering.</br>Comfort is not this scooter's strong suit. If you are expecting a plush, sofa-like ride, you might want to look elsewhere.</br>The biggest culprit? The stiff shock absorbers. Even when the scooter was new, the suspension felt firm; a decade later, it feels downright unforgiving. You will feel every pothole, every speed bump, and every pebble on the road. On long rides, this stiffness translates directly to your lower back and wrists. It’s a "utility-first" machine, and it reminds you of that every time you hit a patch of bad road.</br>The Verdict: A Reliable Workhorse Activa 125 is the "Old Reliable" of the Indian scootering world. It isn't flashy, and it certainly isn't the most comfortable ride in the segment. However, if you value a strong build and a peppy engine that refuses to die, it’s hard to beat. It’s a no-nonsense tool built for the long haul—just maybe invest in a good seat cushion if your daily commute involves broken pavement.

reviews.title: Amazing
reviews.description: It is unavailable to get such a bike at this price; it is amazing. The Honda Dio remains a powerhouse in the 110cc scooter segment, successfully blending aggressive, "moto-scooter" aesthetics with the rock-solid reliability that defines the Honda brand. Designed primarily for a younger demographic, its sharp lines, apron-mounted LED headlamp, and sleek bodywork give it a modern, sporty presence that stands out against more conservative commuter models. At its heart lies a refined 110cc PGM-FI engine, which is remarkably smooth and quiet thanks to the ACG silent start system. While it isn’t built for high-speed racing, it provides a punchy and agile performance for city commutes, paired with an impressive fuel efficiency of around 45–50 kmpl. One of the most significant upgrades in recent iterations is the inclusion of telescopic front suspension and a 12-inch front wheel, which have vastly improved its handling over potholes and uneven urban roads. The scooter is also packed with practical features like an external fuel filler cap, which eliminates the hassle of lifting the seat at petrol pumps, and a side-stand engine cut-off for enhanced safety. Despite its many strengths, the Dio’s lightweight fibre body—while excellent for nimbleness and fuel economy—doesn’t feel as rugged as the metal-bodied Activa and can be prone to minor rattles after years of heavy use on rough roads. Additionally, taller riders might find the floorboard space a bit cramped during long rides. However, these are minor trade-offs for a vehicle that offers such a high resale value and low maintenance costs. Ultimately, the Honda Dio is the definitive choice for college students and urban professionals who want a stylish, easy-to-handle, and dependable machine that makes a statement without breaking the bank. It remains a top-tier contender for anyone prioritising flair and agility in their daily ride.

reviews.title: About my bike
reviews.description: Before I begin this TVS Ntorq 125 review, I must tell you that, growing up, I always hated scooters. I am talking about the ’80s and early ’90s here, which means I am mostly referring to the Vespa clones, such as the Chetak, Super, and Priya. From their miniature wheels to the further dynamically flawed engine placement (side-mounted), I disliked everything about them. I could tolerate the Lambrettas though, as they were not only dynamically sorted comparatively (bigger wheels; engine placed centrally, in line with the chassis, etc.), the pillion comfort was better too, thanks again to the correct placement of the engine, which allowed space for the foot-boards to be extended all the way back making for comfortable footrests for the pillion. There has never been a more comfortable scooter for the pillion. No, the Blaze wasn’t a patch on the Lamby in this aspect

reviews.title: My Daily Ride That Never Disappoints
reviews.description: I’ve been using the TVS NTorq 125 for a while now, and I can honestly say it has become more than just a scooter for me—it’s my daily companion. From office rides to quick city runs, the NTorq has handled everything smoothly without giving me any reason to complain.</br>The first thing you notice is the performance. The pickup is strong and instant, which makes riding in city traffic easy and stress-free. Overtakes don’t feel forced, and the scooter stays stable even when you push it a bit. It feels sporty but still controlled, which is a big plus for everyday riding.</br>Mileage was something I was slightly concerned about at first, but the NTorq surprised me here as well. I’m getting around 40 km per litre, which I feel is very reasonable considering the power it delivers. For a 125cc scooter with this kind of performance, that mileage feels totally worth it.</br>The design is another reason I love this scooter. It looks aggressive, stylish, and definitely stands out on the road. The digital meter feels modern and useful, and the overall build quality feels solid. Even after regular use, there are no unnecessary rattles or issues.</br>Comfort-wise, the seating is good for daily rides, and even longer trips don’t feel tiring. Braking is confident, and the scooter feels safe and predictable on Indian roads.</br>Overall, the TVS NTorq 125 offers a great mix of power, style, comfort, and mileage. For me, it has been a reliable, fun, and satisfying ride, and I genuinely feel it’s one of the best scooters in its segment.

Does it offer similar or better performance than its rivals? And does it set any new benchmarks in the segment? Well, let’s find out.

reviews.title: Avenis is the best for mileage its almost give 60-62 average is ride smooth
reviews.description: The Suzuki Avenis is a sporty and stylish scooter designed mainly for young riders who want both performance and good looks. reviews.title: Best Performance Scooter

Additionally, the seat can be a bit hard, which may not be comfortable for long rides. The slim 10-inch rear tire can feel unstable during high-speed cornering. reviews.title: Smoothy Drive

reviews.title: Overall performance and value of this machine

Now I'm owning this machine for past 15 months and clocked around 17000 kms. Seriously I'm saying that the highest mileage I got around 61.5 during a trip to thrissur from Coimbatore and the least mileage I got as nearly 38 40 on high speed. Normally if you drive in eco mode sure you get 55+ average in city. Coming to the service and maintenance part it is somehow little bit costly that rivals but it feels premium on spending that much amount and the quality is damn superb. The last service bill came for me around 2000 for the  general yearly maintenance which includes spare parts. On my point of view if you are taller person and searching for sportier scooter and also need efficiency it's the better choice for you.

reviews.title: Great scooter, but a missed opportunity from Suzuki.
reviews.description: I don't own this scooter, but I did have some test rides of it, because I wanted to upgrade from my 2015 Swish 125 facelift.</br>THINGS I LIKED: </br>1. STYLING: Since I was looking for a sports-styled body, the Avenis did catch my eye. It is a good-looking, handsome scooter with sharp graphics all over the body. </br>2. FEATURES: Not the best in class features here but you'll find most things that modern scooters get. Bluetooth, Navigation, Disc Brakes, Charging port, it has all those basics covered.</br>3: REFINEMENT: The 125cc Suzuki engine is very refined and reliable. It doesn't transfer unnecessary vibrations to the body. Keep it serviced and you'll have a trouble-free experience in the engine department at least. You can cruise on the highway at 70-75km/h all day and the engine will still run as smoothly as silk.</br>THINGS I DID NOT LIKE:</br>1. THE ELECTRONICS: These issues existed with my Swish 125 as well, and it's sad that they haven't changed their ways in 10 years. If you are coming from a Honda/TVS, you'll know exactly what I mean. The switches and the wiring are not very high quality and you'll see that with time. </br>2. THE BUILD QUALITY: Same goes for the panel fit and finish. The plastic parts are good but the bits that connect them, when they break (which they will after some time), the entire thing could start rattling. Some of these parts are not screwed but they are connected joint-to-joint. These are the places where things can break.</br>3. THE EXPECTATION VS. WHAT YOU GET: My problem is, when I'm looking for a sports scooter, I'm expecting slightly better performance than regular/commuter 125cc scooters. You don't get that here. When TVS did their NTorq, they did not just take a Jupiter 125cc engine and put it in a racy body. They returned the engine, put on bigger wheels, tuned the suspension and put on a different exhaust, making it more powerful, sports-oriented, and different than their Jupiter 125. Hero did the same with their Xoom 125 by making it different from their Destini 125. So you get 14-inch wheels, and a different engine tune, which makes it go from 0-60 in the quickest time. But, has Suzuki made the Avenis different/unique? Naah. It's just a Suzuki Access in different clothing. This would have been fine if it were priced well, but no. It costs just as much as the Xoom or NTorq, and the Avenis underperform both of those. Don't get me wrong, it's still pretty quick, but when you're in a market looking for a sports scooter, I can see why people would overlook the Avenis. Not because its not a good product, but because it isn't offering anything unique to the customer. And since it's just an Access in a different clothing, people end up buying the Access instead, which is cheaper and has the same performance level and features.</br>VERDICT: I like the Avenis. It has the basics right. It will do everything a 125cc scooter should do and it's very, very refined. It handles well, it is quick, comfortable, and it has all the features. But if performance is your top priority, you have better choices at this price point. And Suzuki needs to do something. My 2015 Swish has almost the same power and torque figures as their newer models. They need to wake up and up their engine performance and build quality.

reviews.title: Revving Up the Streets: Aprilia SR 125 Review – Style, Speed, and Substance"
reviews.description: Review of the Aprilia SR 125</br> Buying Experience</br>Purchasing the Aprilia SR 125 is generally a smooth and pleasant experience. Aprilia dealerships are known for their professional and friendly staff who are knowledgeable about their products. They offer comprehensive test rides and detailed explanations of the scooter’s features. Financing options are typically available, making them accessible to a range of buyers. The documentation process is straightforward, and the delivery is usually timely, with the vehicle arriving in excellent condition.</br> Riding Experience</br>Riding the Aprilia SR 125 is an exhilarating experience, particularly for those who appreciate sporty scooters. The SR 125 offers a nimble and agile ride, perfect for urban commuting and occasional longer trips. Its lightweight frame and well-tuned suspension provide excellent handling and stability, even on rough roads. The seating position is comfortable, and the ergonomics are well-suited for both short and long rides. The throttle response is smooth, and the scooter reaches a decent top speed, making it enjoyable for daily use.</br>Looks and Performance</br>The Aprilia SR 125 stands out with its aggressive and sporty design. The sharp lines, bold colors, and sporty decals give it a distinctive and eye-catching appearance. The build quality is robust, and the fit and finish are top-notch. Performance-wise, the SR 125 is powered by a 125cc engine that delivers adequate power for city commuting. The engine is refined, with minimal vibrations, and offers a good balance of power and fuel efficiency. The braking system is efficient, with disc brakes at the front providing excellent stopping power.</br>Servicing and Maintenance</br>Servicing the Aprilia SR 125 is relatively hassle-free. Aprilia has a decent network of service centers, although they may not be as widespread as some competitors. The service staff are generally well-trained and handle maintenance tasks efficiently. Regular servicing costs are reasonable, though some parts might be slightly more expensive due to the premium nature of the brand. However, the overall reliability of the scooter means that major issues are rare and routine maintenance is usually sufficient to keep it running smoothly.</br>Pros and Cons</br>Pros:</br>-Sporty Design: The Aprilia SR 125 has a standout sporty look that appeals to younger riders and those looking for a stylish scooter.</br>-Good Performance: The 125cc engine offers a good blend of power and fuel efficiency, making it ideal for city commuting.</br>- Handling and Stability: Excellent handling and stability make it a joy to ride in various conditions.</br>- Build Quality: High-quality materials and a solid build ensure durability and longevity.</br>Cons:</br>- Service Network: While improving, Aprilia's service network is not as extensive as some other brands, which can be inconvenient in less urban areas.</br>- Spare Parts Cost: Some spare parts can be relatively expensive, reflecting the premium nature of the brand.</br>- Storage Space: Limited under-seat storage compared to some competitors, which can be a drawback for riders who need to carry more items.</br>In summary, the Aprilia SR 125 is a fantastic choice for those seeking a stylish, sporty, and reliable scooter for urban commuting. While it has a few drawbacks, its pros significantly outweigh the cons, making it a worthy contender in the 125cc scooter segment.

Misleading Range Information</br>At the time of purchase, the sales representative clearly stated that the scooter provides a range of 159 km on a full charge. However, after purchasing and charging the vehicle to 100%, the displayed range is only about 125 km. This significant gap between the promised and actual range feels misleading and undermines trust.</br>2. Rapid Battery Drain</br>The battery performance has been another major concern. During real-world usage, the battery is discharging much faster than expected. For approximately 30 km of riding, the battery range drops by around 38 km, which is far from efficient and raises concerns about long-term usability and reliability.</br>3. Poor Delivery Condition</br>To make matters worse, the scooter was delivered with a damaged rear bracket. Receiving a brand-new vehicle in a defective condition reflects poorly on quality control and delivery standards.</br>Overall Impression</br>Due to inaccurate claims, unsatisfactory battery performance, and poor delivery condition, my experience with the Ather Rizta Z has been highly disappointing. reviews.title: Utterly waste of money

During this period, there was no meaningful service carried out on the issues I had reported. The vehicle was returned with only a basic wash/polish. More concerning, the battery level dropped significantly while the vehicle was in the service centre’s custody (from around ~80% when handed over to ~15–20% at delivery). For a vehicle that was not in my use, this raises serious concerns about how customer vehicles are handled.</br>What’s also troubling is that during the initial service, no “issues” were identified. Only later were new concerns suddenly raised, which creates a lack of trust in the diagnostic and quality-check process. It feels inconsistent and reactive rather than thorough and transparent.</br>Customer support has been uncoordinated. Each time I spoke to a different representative, I was asked to repeat my concerns because previous notes were either incomplete or missing. This results in unnecessary delays and frustration, and it does not feel customer-centric. There is no proper handover between support agents, which makes resolution slower than it should be.</br>Overall, while the product itself has good features, the service experience has not met expectations. Repeated delays, unclear diagnostics, poor communication, and concerns about how vehicles are handled during service have seriously impacted my trust. I hope Ather improves service quality, documentation, and accountability at service centres.

reviews.title: Balanced Verdict on Ola S1 Air – A Decent but Compromised EV
reviews.description: The Ola S1 Air is designed as an affordable, feature-packed electric scooter for city riders. It combines modern looks with smart features but comes with noticeable compromises.</br>Positives:</br>The scooter scores well on design with a flat floorboard, roomy under-seat storage, and a sharp, youthful appearance. At just 108 kg, it feels light and agile, making it easy to handle in traffic. The 7-inch touchscreen adds a premium touch with features like ride modes, music, navigation, and proximity unlock, which are rare in this price segment. Range is another plus, with real-world performance between 85–110 km depending on the mode, sufficient for daily commutes.</br>Negatives:</br>Despite these strengths, the S1 Air struggles in critical areas. Braking relies only on drum brakes, which lack bite and stability at higher speeds. Throttle response feels inconsistent, with jerky acceleration and delayed cut-offs, which can be unsettling in stop-go traffic. Prolonged high-speed riding also causes performance throttling due to heat management issues. Build quality isn’t its strongest point either, with basic plastic panels and fit-finish concerns. Additionally, many users report software glitches and slow after-sales support, raising questions about long-term reliability.</br>Verdict:</br>The Ola S1 Air offers a good mix of technology, range, and everyday usability at a competitive price. It is well-suited for urban riders looking for a stylish EV with modern features and decent running costs. However, shortcomings in braking, throttle refinement, and service quality prevent it from being a segment leader.</br>Overall, it’s a scooter that makes sense for budget-conscious riders willing to accept some compromises, but rivals like the TVS iQube and Bajaj Chetak may feel more dependable.</br>Final Rating: 3 out of 5 stars.

expert_reviews.title: TVS iQube: First Ride Review
expert_reviews.description: When it comes to two wheelers, especially scooters, you already have a few EV scooters on sale in the form of Ather and our very own Bajaj with the lovely Chetak. Obviously TVS couldn’t have stayed behind and had recently launched the iQube.

reviews.title: Good and excellent driving experience
reviews.description: The iQube is one of the most popular electric scooters in India and offers a smooth, quiet, and comfortable riding experience, especially for city commuting. Unlike petrol scooters, the iQube runs on an electric motor, so the ride feels very silent and vibration-free. This makes it enjoyable for daily travel in busy urban areas.</br>One of the most noticeable aspects of riding the iQube is its instant acceleration. The electric motor delivers power immediately when the throttle is twisted, allowing the scooter to move quickly in traffic. This quick response helps riders easily overtake vehicles and navigate through congested roads. The scooter’s motor can produce strong torque and reach a top speed of around 75–82 km/h, which is suitable for city rides. </br>The ride comfort of the iQube is also impressive. It comes with telescopic front suspension and rear shock absorbers that absorb bumps and potholes effectively, providing a stable and smooth ride. The seat is wide and comfortable, making it suitable for both the rider and a pillion passenger. In addition, the scooter has a spacious footboard and good build quality, which improves overall comfort during longer.

reviews.title: Best electric scooter out there

The range in eco mode is 105 kms and in sport mode 75 kms. I ride in sport mode majorly coz it's so good in sport mode, fun to drive. Handling is very good, and you feel confident. Seat cushioning is good, and you feel tired only after a very long ride. </br>Pros - </br>storage (better than others)</br>Range (true what the company claims, not like other brands that claim something and deliver something lower)</br>Maintenance free</br>Ride quality </br>Stability </br>Comfort </br>Cons -</br>The biggest con is TVS service centres, and their representatives and mechanics. They don't know anything and don't know how to treat customers. Absolutely pathetic service experience every time. Even at the showroom, they don't attend to you properly if you say you are interested in Iqube. Not sure it's coz they get less profit in Iqube or what's the issue.</br>Navigation - turn-by-turn navigation is just a marketing gimmick. It doesn't work properly </br>Summary: Overall, it's the best EV out there. The pros outweigh the cons by a big margin. TVS needs to increase its service quality and capacity as this is undermining a superb product. It really is a tremendous product, just let down by the TVS staff.

reviews.description: ​While the TVS iQube , I want to highlight a significant issue with the instrument cluster (gauge) that affects the riding experience:</br>​Daytime Glare: The angle and glossy surface of the screen reflect intense sunlight directly into the rider’s eyes. In sunny cities like Hyderabad, this makes it very difficult to see the road and causes eye strain.</br>​Nighttime Brightness: The auto-brightness feature often malfunctions at night, becoming so bright that it is distracting. reviews.title: Nice bike for average ride
reviews.description: Nice scooty for regular use. The Bajaj Chetak is one of the most recognizable names in the Indian two-wheeler market, and its electric version successfully blends heritage with modern technology. Reintroduced as an electric scooter, the Chetak stands out for its premium design, smooth performance, and strong brand value.</br>In terms of design, the Chetak features a retro-modern look with a solid metal body, smooth curves, and a clean finish. The build quality feels premium compared to many other electric scooters in the segment. It comes with stylish LED lighting and a digital instrument cluster that provides essential riding information. The overall fit and finish reflect Bajaj’s focus on durability and quality.</br>Performance-wise, the Chetak is well-suited for city commuting. The electric motor delivers smooth acceleration, especially in urban traffic conditions. It offers a refined and silent riding experience, which is a major advantage of electric vehicles. The scooter feels stable and well-balanced, making it comfortable for daily rides.</br>The riding range typically falls between 90 to 100 km on a single charge, depending on riding style and road conditions. This makes it practical for daily office commutes and short city trips. Charging takes around 4 to 5 hours, which is convenient for overnight charging at home.</br>Comfort is another strong point. The suspension setup handles city roads effectively, and the seating position is upright and relaxed. Braking performance is reliable, adding to rider confidence.</br>Overall, the Bajaj Chetak is a stylish, premium electric scooter ideal for urban riders who value comfort, brand reliability, and smooth performance. reviews.title: Best bike

reviews.title: Discouraged

To make matters worse, the customer service has been unresponsive and unhelpful. I strongly discourage anyone from purchasing this product due to its unacceptable quality and lack of support.

reviews.title: Bad experience with hero electric
reviews.description: Bought hero electric nyx single battery model in oct 2021. Using for daily commute. It has a few faults which am listing down :</br>1. Battery connector plug is very tight and I cannot disconnect the battery and take it outside the scooter for recharging.</br>2. No suspension at all. Zero cushioning effect while going on bad roads. The scooter shakes and jars you in every pothole on the roads.</br>3. The battery charger gets very hot while charging.</br>4. The support stand kept in the rear for keeping bags, is tilted from the time of purchase onwards. Poor quality control.</br>5. The battery charger plug gets stuck in the battery and also in the connector kept outside the scooter in the front. The charger plug will not come out. After much pulling it may come out. Last time it got stuck and till now I cannot remove it. So I have kept the charger connected to the battery and under the seat, permanently now.</br>6. The scooter goes off when braking and especially while going thru bad roads with potholes. It may start automatically after some time and if am not careful the scooter jumps.</br>7. Finally yesterday the scooter stopped after I applied brakes and did not start again. Now it is not running only even though the battery is fully charged and the horns, lights and indicator panel are all working.</br>Am going to give it to the workshop tomorrow.</br>My advice to anyone who is thinking of buying hero electric scooters : do not buy. Waste of money.

expert_reviews.title: River Indie Electric Scooter: First Ride Review
expert_reviews.description: Back in February, we had our first look at the River Indie electric scooter, but that was just the pre-production model. Now, the brand has finally commenced mass production of the Indie and here's what it's like to ride it in the real world.

reviews.title: A SUV in EV's
reviews.description: The River Indie is powered by a robust 4 kWh lithium-ion battery mated to a mid-drive PMSM motor that generates a peak power of 6.7 kW and a maximum torque of 26 Nm, allowing the scooter to reach a top speed of 90 km/h and accelerate from 0 to 40 km/h in just 3.7 seconds. It offers a claimed IDC range of 161 km, though real-world riding in its three modes—Eco, Ride, and Rush—typically yields closer to 120 km on a full charge. The chassis is built around a steel tubular dual-cradle frame supported by 14-inch alloy wheels, telescopic front forks, and twin hydraulic rear shock absorbers, providing a steady ride with a ground clearance of 165 mm. For utility, it leads the segment with 55 litres of total lockable storage, split between a massive 43-litre under-seat bin and a 12-litre front glove box. Safety and tech features include disc brakes at both ends (240 mm front/200 mm rear) with a Combi-Braking System (CBS), a 6-inch high-contrast digital display, and a unique chain-drive system designed for durability and lower long-term maintenance.

reviews.title: Impressive and good road appearance also smooth riding
reviews.description: From the first day of use, it feels awesome. Good look, smooth ride, unique design, big storage make it SUV. It gives more confidence while riding. Front suspension is not upto the mark. River needs to work on it. 14-inch tyres make it stronger and disc braking makes it reliable. Experiencing a good EV revolution.

reviews.title: Great indie
reviews.description: Attractive e-scooter. Praising its style and performance. River Indie electric scooter highlights its strong performance, unique "SUV-like" design, excellent storage (43L boot), and fun ride quality, especially handling bumps well due to its suspension and 14-inch wheels, but users note a stiff front suspension for solo riders, limited cornering clearance, a somewhat flimsy charging flap, and concerns about limited availability/after-sales service in some cities.

reviews.title: I am falling in love with River
reviews.description: The road presence will make anyone fall in love with this scooter. The storage and sitting comfort make it more desirable. It gives a smooth ride and feel proud of being made in India. It's a dream come true.</br>I can only say will be the one whom you will fear to lose.</br>I also expect touch screen, camera,and sensor in future.

reviews.title: Powerful motor
reviews.description: The electric scooty truly stands out because of its powerful motor and impressive on-road performance. From the very first ride, the acceleration feels smooth and responsive. The pickup is quick, which makes it easy to overtake and maintain speed even in busy traffic. What really appreciate is that the scooter doesn't lose power on steep roads or flyovers; the motor continues to pull strongly without any struggle comfortable.

reviews.title: Ride with River is like Flow in River.

Everyone should drive this vehicle and can feel how this works. Price is not a matter when we ride this vehicle and experience it. Thank you for the company.
